sourceReferences.snippet: 13. Are other transit systems experiencing funding challenges or cutting service? Yes. Transit agencies across the country are facing similar budget pressures as pandemic-era funding ends and operating costs continue to rise. In Philadelphia, the San Francisco Bay Area, Washington, D.C.; Chicago; and Portland, this has led to service reductions, lower frequency, or proposed cuts without new funding. While the specifics vary by region, the broader trend is consistent: many transit systems are working to maintain reliable service in the face of long-term funding gaps.

sourceReferences.snippet: A. Overbroad Definition of Non-Protected Speech (Regulation 4392, Section II.B) • The Policy Language: CCSD Regulation 4392 states: "when District employees engage in speech that arises directly from their work, the speech is not protected... speech is considered to arise from an employee's work when the speech concerns a subject matter that primarily involves the employee's job or duties." It further claims that "specific issues, concerns, or grievances regarding a District employee's work are not considered matters of public concern." • The Violation: This definition overreaches Garcetti v. Ceballos. Garcetti applies strictly to speech made pursuant to official job duties (e.g., writing an official internal memo), NOT speech about a workplace topic made in an employee's private capacity. Declaring that anything "involving" a job cannot be a matter of public concern unconstitutionall...

NRS 354.290 requires the County Auditor to report to the Board of Supervisors a statement of revenues and expenditures based on the accounts and funds as were used in the budget. A more detailed accounting is available on the City’s website – www.carson.org.

All billings for dates of service prior to July 1 must be submitted to CITY no later than the first Friday in August of the same year. A billing submitted after the first Friday in August will subject CONSULTANT to an administrative fee not to exceed $100.00. The parties hereby agree this is a reasonable estimate of the additional costs to CITY of processing the billing as a stale claim and that this amount will be deducted from the stale claim payment due to CONSULTANT.

While technological infrastructure is important to economic development, the unique environmental conditions, limited natural resources, and rural community structure of Silver Springs make it an unsuitable location for energy- and water-intensive industrial facilities such as hyperscale data centers. The following concerns are based on current data, state projections, and federal environmental guidance.

sourceReferences.snippet: 60 days. The project is being funded through the High-Speed Nevada Initiative Phase 3 (HSNV3) utilizing capital project funds, state and local fiscal recovery funds. HSNV3 was designed to accelerate broadband deployment in underserved areas through direct infrastructure investment. Mr. Everson showed the board room a map of the area and addresses planned to receive the internet. Laura Shivers in Crescent Valley asked if Crescent Valley would be considered. The board viewed the website that people can use to sign up for the Sky Fiber Internet. Robin Hicks asked about availability to the Townsite of Eureka, Mr. Everson answered that another company received the bid for the town of Eureka but are not projected to begin until 2029. To sign up people will use their website. The board took a 10-minute recess. Chairman McKay called the meeting back to order at 11:06am.

At the time of issuance of bonds authorized pursuant to subsection 4, the board of trustees shall establish a reserve account in its debt service fund for payment of the outstanding bonds of the school district. The reserve account must be established and maintained in an amount at least equal to the lesser of: (a) For a school district located in a county whose population is 100,000 or more, 25 percent; and (b) For a school district located in a county whose population is less than 100,000, 50 percent, of the amount of principal and interest payments due on all of the outstanding bonds of the school district in the next fiscal year or 10 percent of the outstanding principal amount of the outstanding bonds of the school district.

sourceReferences.snippet: 3. Spot Zoning Inconsistencies in the Downtown Mixed Use Expansion If Downtown Mixed Use (DTMU) zoning is planned to extend north to Winnie Lane, there must be consistent application. As currently proposed, John and Corbett Streets are included in the DTMU designation, yet Rice Street—directly between them—is completely excluded without any stated reason. I have raised this issue multiple times at Master Plan review meetings and through the online portal and have yet to receive any explanation. This kind of arbitrary spot zoning raises serious concerns about transparency and fairness in how zoning boundaries are being drawn. Residents deserve consistent and accountable planning—not piecemeal decisions that affect property values and neighborhood character without public justification.
